- Model consistently underestimates prices in early periods (first 5–10 days) and overestimates in late periods (last 5–10 days), suggesting a lag or horizon bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., 80+), model forecasts overshoot and fail to correct downward — exhibit persistent overreaction.
- Mean reversion is not captured: model fails to recognize that prices often return to prior 30-day average after volatility spikes.
- Forecasting horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts tend to be too optimistic in the short term (first 10 days) and too pessimistic in the long term (last 10 days).
- Model exhibits strong bias toward higher prices in the first 10 days of the forecast window, especially when history shows recent upward momentum.
- When history includes a recent sharp decline, model fails to anticipate the continuation or reversal — underestimates the depth of the drop.
- Model does not adjust for seasonal or calendar-based patterns (e.g., end-of-quarter or end-of-month effects) — often misses downward pressure in late periods.
- Forecasting error is more pronounced when true outcome deviates from historical mean — model overreacts to outliers, especially when they are followed by a correction.
